description:
This request concerns the whole of Ridgewood Drive, and more specifically the blind hill that crests around 44-48 Ridgewood Drive, between the Maywood Way and Vistawood Way intersections.  The local residents continue to observe multiple instances of automobiles traveling as unsafe speeds both entering and exiting towards the open space accesses further up the street.  Many have pets and small children, and are concerned for the safety of these loved ones, as well as the general safety of residents on the street.  These conditions make it dangerous to park on the side of the street and to back out of driveways on both sides of the blind hill.  There has been a sign in place warning traffic of the blind hill, and that has not abated the unsafe activity.

We’d like to request the instillation of speed humps on either side of the blind hill in order to curtail travelling at excessive speeds, and increase the safety of pedestrians and residents.  Additionally, we believe speed humps at strategic locations up and down all of Ridgewood (from the Maywood Way intersection to the dead end open space access) would increase the general safety of the neighborhood, as the open space is often frequented by outside residents who may not be as familiar with the road as local residents.

description:
About a year ago, I asked the City of San Rafael to investigate the corner of Ross Valley Avenue and Terrace Avenue, where it appears the road is sinking.  I met a team from San Rafael at the site, who informed me that they were getting bids for the repair and the problem would be cured/repaired in the summer of 2025.  Nothing happened and now we are going into winter.  It is disappointing to be told one thing and then have nothing done.  When will this be repaired.

The other major issue, which I also called on, is on the opposite corner.  In the winter the storm drain is constantly clogged with debris from up the hill.  We end up getting large volumes of rock and dirt that wash around the corner and settle.  I spend hours every year in rain gear, shoveling and removing buckets of debris.  The storm drain catches very little of the water because the space between the bars is narrow and the barrs face the wrong direction.  I have asked this to be repaired as I am tired of being the only one to clear the debris.  When will this be taken seriously and addressed?

title: Trees / árboles
description:
Email rec'd re: tree evaluation(s): "To the Public Works Department .
       In January 2025 , I called from England while I was staying for the holidays and left a message on the telephone to the Public Works Department  about the tree problem on Wolfe Grade  ( San Rafael location ).I also brought it up when I attended a San Pedro Road Collation meeting but no one listened .I was told at that meeting there were only 12 tree workers for San Rafael and they could not get around to everything ...also brought it up with the County Supervisor at that meeting but she said bring it up with San Rafael which I did .
        I travel over Wolfe Grade most  days from my office in Greenbrae and there is a tree waiting to crash down on a passing cars .As you come over the Grade from the Sloat Garden Center it is within  the jurisdiction of San Rafeal .The tree is on the right side on a bend and it is leaning right in to the road , soddened with all the rain ,saturated at the roots ,can quickly and with out warning crash to the ground .I know , have many trees on my property and last year went to Novato at 2pm and when I returned two hours later a huge tree had crashed to the ground ..just suddenly crashed to the ground uplifted by the roots .This tree in particular is on private property , I think , but the owners must be aware of the liability and some one needs to something about it before it is too late .The reason I had called to warn about the trees on Wolf Grade from England was when  two people had been killed when trees fell on their cars in two separate incidences in heavy rains that had just occurred in England .So hence my warning .There are other trees on this section of the road on both sides that should be evaluated for safety reasons to on going traffic .
         The whole of Wolfe Grade needs to be traveled on both sides to understand what I mean .Also, the whole of D Street should be evaluated as there are so many tree branches entwined amongst the PG&E wires and the traffic light at Bayview Street is completed obliterated  by a tree in front of 340 D Street ...so when you are coming from the Greenbrae side you have to get almost upon the light before you see it .I hope some one will take it upon themselves to quickly go and look at the tree I am talking about and will take immediate action as one owes it to the public ,thank you for your time on reading this and I hope I will get a reply "

location.address: Wolfe Grade San Rafael, California, 94901

category: Trees / árboles

description:
A pedestrian was just killed at Second and A, the second traffic death this month?  Do you all realize the pedestrian walk signs have changed? They no longer indicate walk unless someone activates the sensor well before the light changes. This means when people approach the intersection and cross WITH the light as they should, the walk signal is still indicating to drivers a non-walk signal. This gets people killed. 

Also - We reported the lack a red light wait time on 3rd and A months ago when new lights were installed, meaning all signals should be in red in both directions before one turns green (typically only a few seconds).  These lights change simultaneously which led to 4 serious accidents in a 24 hour period. We commented on this problem then but nothing has changed.  This is such a simple programming change - why is it not fixed? Our staff won't even cross the street at 3rd and A, it's still too dangerous.

No traffic calming measures will ever change anything is your signals are not properly set. The city seriously needs to get their traffic consultant to remedy these issues immediately or more people will die.

Michael Eisenmenger - michael@cmcm.tv

Email rec'd from resident re: installing pedestrian activated warning system at crosswalk:

"Dear City of San Rafael Public Works Department,
I am writing as a concerned resident of Terra Linda to formally request a safety review and the installation of an enhanced, pedestrian-activated warning system at the existing crosswalk on Del Ganado Road.
Location Details:
•	Street: Del Ganado Road
•	Exact Crosswalk Location: The existing crosswalk spanning Del Ganado Road, located between approximately 756 Del Ganado Road and 769 Del Ganado Road.
Requested Improvement: I request that the City conduct a traffic safety study (warrants analysis) for this specific location to determine the feasibility of installing a solar-powered, Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) system or an equivalent pedestrian-activated warning sign and push-button.
Justification for Enhancement: This crosswalk is in a heavily residential section of Terra Linda and experiences consistent pedestrian usage, including families, seniors, and students. Due to the road characteristics and vehicle speeds in the area, there are significant visibility concerns that lead to frequent near-miss incidents. A standard crosswalk is not sufficient to warn approaching drivers effectively. The solar-powered, push-button system (RRFB) is crucial for:
1.	Significantly increasing driver awareness of pedestrians attempting to cross.
2.	Improving pedestrian confidence and safety at this neighborhood crossing.
3.	Providing a sustainable, low-maintenance solution (solar power).
I urge the Traffic Division to prioritize this location for an immediate safety review. I would appreciate information on the next steps in the request process and the timeline for a traffic study at this intersection.
Thank you for your attention to this critical public safety matter."

title: Traffic/ Traffic Signal / Tránsito/Señal
description:
Email rec'd re: timing of traffic signals along 2nd & 3rd streets: "Like thousands of others, I regularly drive from Fairfax to San Rafael and back.

 After the light finally turns green going east at the San Anselmo Hub, there is almost always a red light at the next light by the grocery store and Equator Coffee.  After that, on the Miracle Mile, the lights are irregular. Once 2nd Street begins, there are perhaps eight to ten lights to 101 and under 101. Those lights are not timed to match the speed limit or regular traffic flow.  It is virtually impossible to catch green lights all the way to the freeway, then under the freeway. 
The same problem exists heading west on 3rd Street.  There are glitches going from under the freeway, where we often get stopped before and at the Transportation Center, (not counting when trains are present), where there are three (?) lights before Lincoln.  Once past Lincoln, everything  flows well until we hit that new light just past the big city parking light on 3rd, which is not timed to the rest of the lights. After that, the lights are good until a couple of blocks before the merge with 4th Street and the beginning of the Miracle Mile. The two lights that are just  before the merge are usually red.

If 2nd and 3rd Streets were timed to the traffic flow, there would be a big savings on gas from not having to stop and start, and a resulting reduction in pollution.  I would hate to be one of the people who work and/or live between 2nd and 3rd, exposed to the pollution from those thousands of cars every day, all day.

There are some other areas that could benefit from the timing of lights, like near the main Post Office, but to me, 2nd and 3rd Streets are the most constant in my life and I would appreciate a smoother flow of traffic.  Thank you for your attention.  "

location.address: 2nd St San Rafael, California, 94901

category: Traffic/ Traffic Signal / Tránsito/Señal

I serve as the Director of Education at Canal Alliance, a community-based organization located in San Rafael. I commute daily from San Francisco and frequently cross the intersection at 2nd Street and the northbound U.S. 101 offramp, near the Shell gas station.

I’m writing to report a serious pedestrian safety concern at this intersection. Vehicles frequently run the red light and make right turns despite the “No Right Turn on Red” signal. I have witnessed numerous near-collisions between cars and pedestrians—including several instances where I was almost struck while crossing eastbound on 2nd Street.

This intersection presents an immediate danger to pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers alike. I respectfully request that the City consider increased traffic enforcement, review of red-light camera data, or adjustments to signal timing and signage to improve compliance and pedestrian safety.

Thank you for your attention to this important issue. I would be happy to provide additional details or speak with a member of your traffic engineering or public safety team to discuss possible solutions."

Dear Public Works Department,
Why are there so many derelict and abandoned boat docks in front of buildings along the San Rafael Canal?
Can San Rafael please start requiring apartment owners and homeowners to either maintain them or remove their abandoned docks? 
Those old & neglected docks are falling apart and adding debris and toxins to our San Rafael Canal! They are also adding hazards to navigation as they deteriorate. 
Why do the police boats and sheriff boats that go by not see this sort of decay and report it? 
We live on the Canal and frequently witness debris and foam and wood floating by.
If this sort of junk was on the streets of San Rafael, it would be considered blight and removal required!
Please consider this matter and the health of our waterway that leads into wonderful San Francisco Bay!

description:
Email rec'd re: suggestion to install reflectors/lights or some other visible markers:"
I am writing to bring to your attention a safety concern on Sir Francis Drake Blvd near Andersen Drive, just after the 101 South Francis exit, heading toward Marin. The incident occurred where the bike lane is on the right side and there is a sidewalk in the middle, before the lane heads  toward Larkspur before the Anderson Drive in right around there where you couldn’t make a right to Anderson to go straight. The issue is when you go straight here there’s no lights and it’s hard to see the raised sidewalk between the bike laying on the road. My tire hit the curb and I had to invest in a new used car towing my car and I also noticed a lot of other car parts there and people told me they almost wiped out there as well and they saw other parts there that we’re not only mine.

There is debris from multiple vehicles scattered around the curb between the car lane and the bike lane. The curb lacks proper reflectors or lighting, making it difficult to see, especially at night or in low visibility. Even the police report I got I reviewed and it shows that they were no lights and it was dark there.This area appears hazardous and may have been the site of multiple accidents.

For the safety of drivers and cyclists, I recommend installing reflectors, lights, or other visible markers on or near the curb to improve visibility and help prevent further accidents.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.
Sincerely, A Concerned Resident

Although I would just submit this as anonymous, I want to please get a confirmation that you read and receive this email."

title: Vegetation Fire Hazard / Un Peligro de Incendio de Vegetación
description:
If you walk up from the trail head and take the path to the right, you will see the area in the photo just before the short trail dead ends. 
It appears that someone—possibly kids setting up makeshift mountain biking structures or perhaps individuals establishing a temporary encampment—have been constructing ramps and tying ropes around trees in this area.
This raises several safety and liability concerns:
•	The terrain is steep and unstable, making it extremely unsafe for biking or other recreational structures.
•	If it is an encampment, there is an elevated fire risk. We had a fire in this same area a few years ago that originated from a homeless encampment.
•	From a liability perspective, if someone is seriously injured on City property, there is potential exposure to claims against the City.
Given these risks, we wanted to bring this to your attention as soon as possible so the City can assess and determine any appropriate next steps to ensure public safety and protect the property.

description: The lights on Heatherton and Tamalpias and Lincoln between Mission Ave. And 2nd street are an absolute mess and have been since the SMART train began operations. This is creating a safety issue for pedestrians and drivers as frustrated and confused drivers are driving recklessly and erratically to try to ensure they make it through the intersections when their light is green or yellow, and sometimes even when it’s red since the lights cycle through without all lanes of traffic getting a turn sometimes. Additionally this is causing traffic to back up on all the surrounding surface streets, hurting the local residents and businesses because it makes San Rafael a less pleasant and convenient place to drive in or through. Traffic also backs up onto the freeway in both directions exacerbating the traffic issue the train was approved to help alleviate. How and why this has not been addressed and resolved by now is beyond comprehension. If timing the lights correctly is not possible, the train should be forced to stop for traffic signals as was the original intent and the reason the trains are short enough to fit inside a city block without obstructing traffic in either direction.

title: Suggested Improvement/Change / Sugerencias de mejoras/cambios
description:
Email rec'd from resident requesting reduction of traffic speed on Spinnaker Point Dr:

"The project to reduce traffic speed on Spinnaker Point Drive between Catalina Boulevard and Bedford Cove is greatly needed. 
  
I live at 6 Bedford Cove, so I see the traffic on Spinnaker Point Drive every day.  Both residents of Spinnaker Point, and vehicles from outside the community, drive far too fast on the segment between Bedford Cove and Catalina Boulevard. 
  
The very small traffic circle at the intersection of Catalina and SPD is useless.  It's too small and there is no structure, just a few cones and a sign.  Even if a structure were built on the current footprint, it wouldn't work.  I myself see every day that vehicles, both cars and trucks, ignore the circle.  They just turn left, without even stopping unless there is oncoming traffic. 
  
My recommendations: 
  
1.  Remove the traffic circle. 
  
2.  Add speed humps at Rockport Cove, and between Rockport and Newport.  Ones similar to those at the Marin Sanitary Service, or the newest ones on Catalina, would work well.

description:
Re: addition of STOP signs in Gerstle Park at the northeastern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Marin Street, and its counterpart at the southwestern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Lodge Lane.

Please, please, please consider adding STOP signs (not lights) in Gerstle Park on the corners as described on San Rafael Avenue, at the very busy and dangerous intersection at Marin Street and Lodge Lane. 

I have lived at this intersection for almost 9 years and during that time from my kitchen window I have seen a constant stream of dog walkers, preschool groups, elderly pedestrians, parents with strollers, and bicyclists cross there to get to and from the Park--all day, every day, all year round. 

At the same time, civilian drivers (including FedEx & UPS) speed along SR Avenue all day long because there are no stops signs on SR Avenue and it's a wider street (compared to nearby Bayview and Ross streets).

I have seen (and heard) countless near-miss accidents happen at this intersection. This is true especially as cars are driving westbound on SR Ave as the sun is setting (like after work) and their visibility is diminished. Drivers cannot see pedestrians in the crosswalk there until it is too late. 

This specific issue has been posted and commented about by several other neighbors on NextDoor so I wanted to submit an official request on your site today. 

In an unscientific poll, the neighborhood response indicates support for the addition of STOP signs at the northeastern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Marin Street, and its counterpart at the southwestern corner of San Rafael Avenue at Lodge Lane.

Thank you for your strong consideration and I hope to receive periodic updates/responses via email as my request is being processed through your system.

Sincerely,
Adrienne Biggs
Gerstle Park resident/GPNA Member since 1999

description:
I am writing to you concerning the new signage regarding turning from West End Avenue on to Second Street at Marquard Ave. In your plan you say “vehicles from West End Ave (eastbound) can make a right turn only onto Marquard Ave. Vehicles on West End Ave can access Second St through the signalized intersection at Greenfield Ave and Fourth St.  Advanced signage will be installed along Greenfield Ave to direct vehicles to Fourth St for access to Second St towards Downtown San Rafael.”
My husband and I have lived here on Spring Grove Avenue for more than 50 years and have never had a problem merging on to Second Street from West End Avenue. Although I applaud the safe new bike path, I see no reason for traffic not to continue to merge from West End Avenue on to Second Street as it has always done. Also, it makes no sense that vehicles from Marquard can use this intersection and vehicles from West end cannot.   I like the addition of the traffic light as it makes the merger even safer. Unfortunately, over the past several months, I have seen many people ignore this signage.
You’ve also created a new problem with directing people to use the lights at Greenfield and Fourth. Only one car can safely wait at the light. Cars come from three directions and bicycles from two directions. You have created a new dangerous intersection.  If you miss the light allowing cars to turn from Greenfield to Fourth,  you must wait several minutes thus increasing the blockage in the intersection. You have created a new situation that may increase city liability. 
My solution to this problem is to simply remove the signage at Marquard and West End along with the speed bump\barrier in the street. Let cars safely merge with the traffic on Second Street as they have done during the last 50 years I have lived here. 
Respectfully submitted,
Janie Teitelbaum

description:
Email rec'd re: ped signals @ 3rd St and A. St. not working properly

"Based on your attached (below my signature block) email, I thought I could assume that today, when I went to the Kaiser facility on Third Street in San Rafael, I would find all of the "accessible" ped signals operating, and each ped signal's "finder tone" operating as required - being able to be heard "on approach" from 6 to 10 feet away from the actual signal location.

Well, what a surprise!  The "accessible" ped signal on the South East corner of Third Street (see photo) had no "finder tone"!  As I'm sure you know, those "finder tones" are not only there to help a blind/low visioned pedestrian to find the ped signal controller, they are also important because if working, those finder tones can help a blind person cross an intersection.  Once the pedestrian is given the "Walk" statement and starts to cross the intersection, they then can use the finder tone from the signal they are walking to as a guide to help them cross the intersection and reach the far corner safely.  When the finder tone is not working, or the finder tone sound level is too low, they don't have that important safety tool available to them.

The fact that the accessible pedestrian signals located on Third Street and "A" Street are still not working as required is a statement, and not a positive statement as to the City of San Rafael's interest in its responsibilities relating to both physical and "programmatic" access as required by both state and federal access codes and Standards"

description:
I was proceeding north on Grand from 3rd Street in light but steadily moving traffic. As I turned right onto 4th Street I hit a curb on an island that I did not see. Both my front and rear tires hit the curb and went over the island and came down with a heavy thud. I could not see what I had hit as I looked back in my rear view mirror, so I parked and walked back to see if I had damaged anything other than my (newly purchased) tires.

When I walked back to see what I had hit, it became very clear from  the damage to the curb I was not the first to hit it. This is a very busy intersection, not only with auto/bike/pedestrian traffic, but the design itself is very busy and unusual in San Rafael and most of Marin County. 

I firmly suggest that you remove this akward obstacle, or at least paint it’s curbs a bright yellow so it can be seen. The raw concrete is very difficulty to see against the blacktop and with the all the other lines and symbols drawing one’s attention.

As I was driving home following the incident, my car was pulling to the right, so much so that my radar could not keep it in the center of my driving lane. Tomorrow, I will take my car to be inspected and to have a wheel alignment. I will file a claim for the cost of correcting my vehicle. It would be helpful and very much appreciated if you could advise to whom I should present my claim.

I kindly urge you to consider this request. Your prompt attention to this matter is greatly appreciated, and I sincerely hope that by taking proactive measures, we can prevent any potential accidents or injuries.

description:
I was just reading through these articles.
https://www.cityofsanrafael.org/canal-broadband-project-highlights-digital-divide-in-the-community/
https://www.cityofsanrafael.org/canal-wifi-and-digital-equity-in-san-rafael/

I'm slightly baffled at why there is money being wasted researching this in 2022-2024.
I worked off of Mill Street in 2011-2014, our site only had access to 2.4Mb internet from ATT because the central office was over 15,000' from our location. I resorted to using my personal cellphone connection hotspot because it was so bad. We were 100' to far from the Comcast drop to get comcast.

I began working for Marin computers for a summer in 2015 they had comcast buisiness, but it was unreliable due to congestion. I've returned to work at Marin computers recently at 91 Louise St. And we can no longer get comcast due to over subscription. ATT still hasn't rolled out any fiber optic huts to the neighborhood, so they're not an option. Our only option is T-Mobile cellular data and it suffers from peak hour congestion to the point that our VOIP phones become un-usable. Yet the ATT storage yard is on the corner of our street where they house all of their service trucks and fiber spools.

I find it outrageous that money is being wasted confirming the issue exists when all that needs to happen is communicating with the providers. Internet is no longer a luxury niche product. It is critical infrastructure for business and daily life.

Why has there not been a push to deploy updated network infrastructure in this community over 10 years ago? It is extremely densely populated, a new apartment complex is scheduled to be built and it has mid 1990's grade internet access.

Why is the city wasting money researching whether this is a problem that needs to be addressed?
When is infrastructures scheduled to be installed? Will independent providers like SONIC be engaged in the discussion?

description: We live on Wilson and find that at certain times of day, it is very unsafe to pull out of our street onto Lincoln. The lack of visibility for seeing speeding vehicles is compounded by a couple parking spots that are not marked with red curbs on Lincoln that further restrict visibility for this intersection. Since moving to Wilson Ct less than 6 years ago, we have seen over 12 accidents at or just adjacent to our intersection from people pulling out of our street, people who are speeding and hit parked vehicles, etc.   Farther south on Wilson, the speed limit is 25 MPH. This speed limit should be carried all the way north to the 101S-bound Lincoln Ave exit to make the street safer. Open to other suggestions to make our intersection easier and safer to pull out of but at the very least, please carry 25MPH to our cross street.
